skill.title: Find where a function is increasing/decreasing for all x or on intervals
needs: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing at a point

steps.title: Choose the range where f'(x) is negative

lines.text: The graph of $6x^2 - 42x + 40$ is a U-shape, so it is negative between the roots.

skill.title: Find the slope of a tangent to a circle by differentiation

steps.title: Think about the graph of $f(x) + a$

lines.text: Adding $a$ moves the graph of $f$ up (or down) by $a$. A cubic has only one real root when it crosses the $x$-axis once: either the local maximum is below the axis, or the local minimum is above it.

steps.title: Use the number of turning points

lines.text: $T'(x) = 0$ at only one value of $x$ in $[0, 8]$, so the graph has exactly one turning point.
Graphs A and B each have a minimum followed by a maximum (two turning points), so reject them. The answer is C or D.
$x = 0$ means kayak $S$ to $A$, then run $A$ to $F$.
$x = 8$ means kayak straight from $S$ to $F$ (about $82$ minutes).
$T(0) = 1 < 1.37 \approx T(8)$, so the graph ends higher than it starts.
Of C and D, the one that finishes above its starting height is D.

skill.title: Sketch/match the graph of f′ from f
skill.example: turning points of f ↔ roots of f′
needs: Find where a function is increasing/decreasing for all x or on intervals

steps.title: Read the gradient of p(x) at key points

lines.text: The value of $p'(x)$ is the gradient of $p(x)$.
At $x = 1$ and $x = 3$, $p(x)$ has a turning point, so the gradient is $0$: $p'(1) = 0$ and $p'(3) = 0$.
$p(x)$ is steepest uphill at its inflection point $x = 2$, where the gradient is at its maximum, so $p'(2) = 1$.

steps.title: Use the shape of p'(x) to find the last point

lines.text: $p(x)$ is a cubic, so $p'(x)$ is a quadratic: a U-shape upside down, with its peak at $(2, 1)$.
A quadratic is symmetric about its peak, so $x = 4$ matches $x = 0$: $p'(4) = -3$.

steps.title: Plot the points and join them

lines.text: Plot $(0, -3)$, $(1, 0)$, $(2, 1)$, $(3, 0)$ and $(4, -3)$, then draw a smooth curve through them.
